 Petrol, diesel cheaper in India than Dubai? Check city-wise prices and why the gap exists | Explained
 Delhi's diesel price is nearly Rs 28 per litre lower than Dubai's, while petrol in Delhi and Noida is also cheaper than Dubai's Special 95 grade. But motorists in Mumbai, Kolkata and Hyderabad pay more for petrol than consumers in Dubai. 
 Moneycontrol World Desk 
 October 22, 2026 / 16:22 IST 
 Story continues below Advertisement

 (FILES) People line up to fill their vehicles with petrol at a fuel station in New Delhi, India, August 3, 2026. REUTERS/Bhawika Chhabra 
 Following recent UAE fuel price hikes, diesel is now cheaper in six major Indian cities than in Dubai, while petrol prices vary with Delhi remaining cheaper than Dubai but Mumbai and Hyderabad being more expensive. Did our AI summary help?

 Motorists in several Indian cities are paying less for petrol and diesel than consumers in Dubai, according to fuel prices as of October 22, 2026. The difference is particularly large for diesel, with Delhi's retail price nearly Rs 28 per litre below the rate in Dubai.
 The comparison follows an increase in fuel prices across the United Arab Emirates (UAE) from October 1. The country's fuel-pricing committee raised rates for all three petrol grades and diesel, pushing Dubai's prices above those in several Indian cities.
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 However, fuel costs differ significantly across India because of state taxes and other local charges. Petrol in Mumbai, Kolkata and Hyderabad, for instance, is more expensive than Dubai's Special 95 grade.
 Petrol prices: Delhi cheaper than Dubai, but not every Indian city 
 Dubai's Special 95 petrol costs AED 4.28 per litre, equivalent to approximately Rs 110.04 at an exchange rate of Rs 25.71 per dirham.
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 Delhi's petrol price stands at Rs 102.12 per litre, while Noida charges Rs 101.96. At these rates, petrol in Delhi is around Rs 7.92 per litre, or 7.2%, cheaper than Dubai's Special 95.

 Dubai offers two other petrol grades. E-Plus 91, its least expensive option, costs AED 4.21 per litre, equivalent to approximately Rs 108.24. Super 98, the premium grade, is priced at AED 4.40, or around Rs 113.12 per litre.
 The picture changes when other Indian cities are considered.
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 Chennai's petrol price is below Dubai's E-Plus 91 grade, while Mumbai and Kolkata are more expensive than Dubai's Special 95. Hyderabad has the highest petrol price among the Indian cities listed.
 The comparison also involves different fuel grades, which may not have identical octane ratings.
 Diesel prices: Delhi pays nearly Rs 28 less per litre 
 The difference is wider for diesel. Dubai's diesel price is AED 4.80 per litre, equivalent to approximately Rs 123.41 at the stated exchange rate.
 Delhi's diesel price is Rs 95.20 per litre, while Noida charges Rs 95.44. This puts the difference at Rs 28.21 per litre for Delhi and Rs 27.97 for Noida.
 In percentage terms, diesel in Delhi costs approximately 23% less than in Dubai.
 Other Indian cities also have lower diesel prices than Dubai, although the gap varies.
 Even in Hyderabad, where diesel costs Rs 104.23 per litre, the price remains approximately Rs 19.18 below Dubai's rate.
 The comparison shows that diesel is cheaper in all six Indian cities listed, while the position for petrol varies from city to city.
 Why did Dubai raise fuel prices in October? 
 The latest price gap follows a sharp increase in UAE fuel rates at the beginning of October.
 On September 30, the UAE's Gasoline and Diesel Prices Follow-up Committee approved revised rates for the month. The changes raised petrol prices by around 16% across the three grades, while diesel prices increased by approximately 11.6%.
 The revised rates were:
 The UAE's official Emirates News Agency, WAM, reported that the revised prices were approved under the country's monthly fuel-pricing mechanism. The system takes global energy prices into account alongside domestic market requirements.
 Volatility in international energy markets and tensions in the Middle East have also raised concerns about possible disruptions to oil supplies.
 The October rates came into effect on October 1. The committee was expected to announce the November prices towards the end of October, with any revisions taking effect from November 1.
 Who decides petrol and diesel prices in Dubai? 
 The UAE follows a monthly fuel-pricing system overseen by the Gasoline and Diesel Prices Follow-up Committee.
 The mechanism was introduced in 2015, when the country moved away from government-subsidised petrol prices towards a system linked to international markets.
 The committee reviews fuel prices towards the end of each month, taking account of international petroleum prices and domestic operating requirements. Its approved rates apply across the UAE, including Dubai and Abu Dhabi, for the designated month.
 The committee's original framework included representatives from the energy and finance ministries, along with senior executives from ADNOC Distribution and Emirates National Oil Company (ENOC).
 This monthly review means fuel prices in the UAE can change from one month to the next as market conditions evolve.
 How are fuel prices determined in India? 
 India follows a different system. Public-sector oil marketing companies, including Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited, determine retail petrol and diesel prices under a market-linked framework.
 The country introduced daily fuel price revisions in June 2017. The system allows oil marketing companies to adjust retail rates in response to changes in international fuel prices and other costs.
 However, prices do not necessarily change every day. Rates can remain unchanged for extended periods even when global crude oil prices fluctuate.
 Taxation is another major factor behind the difference in retail prices between Indian cities. The final price paid by consumers includes central excise duty, state-level value-added tax (VAT), dealer commissions and other costs.
 Since state VAT rates vary, the same fuel can cost considerably more in one city than another.
 This helps explain why petrol in Delhi and Noida is cheaper than Dubai's Special 95, while consumers in Mumbai, Kolkata and Hyderabad pay more. Diesel, meanwhile, remains cheaper in all the Indian cities examined than in Dubai at the prices prevailing on October 22, 2026.
